primary_claim: METR's pre-deployment evaluation measured GPT-5's 50% time horizon on agentic software engineering tasks at ~2h17m (up from o3's 1h30m), and concluded that GPT-5 and near-term incremental development are unlikely to pose catastrophic risk via AI R&D automation, rogue replication, or strategic sabotage threat models, finding no significant evidence of sandbagging despite some situational awareness in reasoning traces

effect.metric: 50% time horizon on agentic software engineering tasks

stated_future_work: baseline some of the hardest HCAST tasks that currently lack human baselines, to increase confidence in results
develop more careful measurement of inference/token-budget scaling for future models
develop more robust monitors and broader honeypot coverage for reward hacking and sandbagging
develop more realistic evaluation environments so models cannot easily tell they are not in real deployment
research targeted finetuning methods to provide assurances against sandbagging without overfitting to evaluations
limitations_stated: GPT-5 is close to saturating many HCAST tasks, and a disproportionate share of the hardest tasks lack human baselines
monitors for reward hacking and sandbagging miss many examples of misbehavior; honeypot experiments are ad-hoc with limited coverage
evaluations are not fully realistic and GPT-5 can often tell it isn't in a real deployment scenario
time horizon is a rough proxy for sandbagging/sabotage ability, and it is unclear what score would be concerning
qualitative assessments of reasoning-trace monitorability could be fooled by a sufficiently capable system
quote: The observed 50%-time horizon of GPT-5 was 2h17m (65m - 4h25m 95% CI) – compared to OpenAI o3’s 1h30m.
